The Blazor Web App is ready. Here's what was built:

**Architecture: Interactive WebAssembly with server prerendering**
- Fast first load via server-side prerendering (static HTML rendered on server)
- After WASM loads, all interaction runs client-side — no server round-trips for UI (ideal for worldwide users with latency)
- Per-page `@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly` on interactive pages

**Key components:**
| Layer | What |
|-------|------|
| `ShipmentTracker.Client/Models/` | Shared `Shipment` model + `ShipmentStatus` enum |
| `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/Track.razor` | Public tracking page (enter tracking #, see status + ETA + progress bar) |
| `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/MyShipments.razor` | Authenticated customers see their shipments |
| `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/Dispatcher.razor` | Dispatchers: create shipments, filter, update status |
| `ShipmentTracker/Endpoints/` | Minimal API endpoints for CRUD |
| `ShipmentTracker/Services/` | Server-side EF Core service |
| Identity + Roles | `Dispatcher` and `Customer` roles seeded at startup |

**Auth:** ASP.NET Core Identity with individual accounts, roles serialized to WASM via `SerializeAllClaims`.

Run with: `dotnet run --project ShipmentTracker`
